v0.2.0-poc.analogy: You plug your PC into the host's LAN with one cable and one password, from wherever you are.
v0.2.0-poc.concept: Overlay mesh (Nebula) and remote node join: a machine on any network becomes a Kubernetes node over an encrypted tunnel.
v0.2.0-poc.real_world: Branch offices, rented GPUs and hybrid home and cloud nodes that join a cluster even behind NAT.
v0.2.0-poc.seen_in: v0.2.0-poc: an AWS machine follows JOIN.md, joins and is Ready in 2 min 30 s.

v0.2.0-poc.analogy: A locker with a timer: you get a key, and it stops working when the hour is over.
v0.2.0-poc.concept: Automated admission with leases: a rule approves and the access expires by itself, so nobody keeps standing access.
v0.2.0-poc.real_world: Edge nodes, partners and ephemeral CI runners that get access just in time and lose it with no one to remember.
v0.2.0-poc.seen_in: v0.2.0-poc: a stranger asks on the page, is approved in 55 s and is expelled at the end of its 1 h lease.

v0.2.0-poc.analogy: Every player gets a room with a lock: free to rearrange it, forbidden to open the others.
v0.2.0-poc.concept: Multi-tenancy: one namespace per player with RBAC, Pod Security, quota and NetworkPolicy; outside it the answer is 403.
v0.2.0-poc.real_world: An internal platform where many teams share one cluster without seeing each other.
v0.2.0-poc.seen_in: v0.2.0-poc: the visitor runs a pod in its own namespace and gets 403 listing nodes.

v0.2.0-poc.analogy: A reception desk that takes your name but has no keys; the envelope with the key comes from the back office.
v0.2.0-poc.concept: A public front door that holds no credential: a visitor asks, waits and collects a sealed bundle from the host's own tick.
v0.2.0-poc.real_world: Self-service onboarding for outside users or partners without giving the web tier any secret.
v0.2.0-poc.seen_in: v0.2.0-poc and v0.2.1-poc: the request page and this What's new page, served by a server with no credential.

v0.2.0-poc.analogy: A player's badge opens his own seat; it cannot rewrite the seating chart.
v0.2.0-poc.concept: Least privilege for a node's own credentials: a node agent's token must not be able to forge another node's identity.
v0.2.0-poc.real_world: Edge or rented nodes you do not fully control, where each agent's token is scoped to what that agent needs.
v0.2.0-poc.seen_in: v0.2.0-poc: the Cilium agent's token can no longer forge another node's endpoints, WireGuard key or identities.

v0.2.0-poc.analogy: The doorman may check the guest list, but he gets no key to the offices.
v0.2.0-poc.concept: Scoped RBAC for a node agent: the SPIRE agent's token may get nodes and pods and nothing more.
v0.2.0-poc.real_world: Any agent that runs on a node you do not fully trust: give it the exact verbs it needs, and nothing cluster-wide.
v0.2.0-poc.seen_in: v0.2.0-poc: the SPIRE agent's token may get nodes and pods, and nodes/proxy is refused (poc-vm V103).

v0.3.0-poc.concept: Mutual consent: a declarative NetworkPolicy opens only after both sides say yes, which is zero trust between tenants.
v0.3.0-poc.real_world: Two teams or companies sharing one service for a limited time, with no ticket to the platform team.
v0.3.0-poc.seen_in: v0.3.0-poc: romero invites carmack, carmack accepts, and only then the Doom match starts.
